items.title: Habtamu Fikadu, Chelbesa, Ethiopia - Washed Process
items.excerpt:
An incredibly complex version of the classic Chelbesa/Guji flavor profile.

Habtamu Fikadu, Ethiopia

Tasting notes: Orange blossom, lemon meringue, hojicha, peach fruit leather, raspberry

Elevation: 2,000+ masl

Variety: Heirloom

Process: Washed

Region: Chelbesa, Guji

Habtamu Fikadu Aga (trading as Kuri Mountain Coffee) was founded in 2015 by Aaga Dinsa, the grandson of a coffee
farmer in Kuri Kebele. He inherited his grandfather’s farm, which remains the export-hub of the operation. Today the
organization spans 105 hectares planted in Kuri Kebele, plus 837 hectares total including the farms of 144 registered
outgrowers. These outgrowers deliver cherry to washing stations owned or managed by the company across Wolega,
Guji, and Jimma.

At the company’s washing stations, cherries are pulped and undergo a submerged fermentation lasting 48–72 hours
depending on temperature. After washing, the parchment rests in water for another 12 hours before being dried on raised beds for 10–12 days. This careful and consistent method underpins the quality across all of Habtamu’s lots.
The company is certified organic (Ecocert) and holds Fair for Life certification. Through Fair for Life, they contribute US
$0.12 per pound on exports plus 5% of company profits into a development fund, which is reinvested locally (in food,
clothing, schooling, roads, health care facilities & equipment). Until 2017, they sold via ECX; now, they export directly.

items.title: Bogalech Dukkale, Ethiopia
items.excerpt:
Bogalech Dukkale — Ethiopia

Tasting Notes: Fruit Punch, Pineapple, Jasmine
Origin: Sidamo, Ethiopia
Producer: Bogalech Dukkale
Variety: Ethiopia Heirloom
Process: Natural
Elevation: 2,180 MASL

A beautiful coffee. A meaningful relationship. A commitment to the years ahead.

Bogalech Dukkale returns to Vivid Coffee for a second year, marking an important milestone in our sourcing relationships. This is the first Ethiopian coffee to join our Relationship Coffee category, reflecting our commitment to purchasing from Bogalech year after year.

Bogalech is a 45-year-old mother of six who, alongside her husband, manages a four-hectare coffee farm in Ethiopia’s Sidamo region. She inherited the land from her parents, continuing a family tradition of coffee farming across generations. Through our importing partner, Osito, and their longstanding relationship with Sookoo, we have the opportunity to purchase her coffee as a distinct, single-farm lot.

This year, we purchased precisely half of Bogalech’s harvest, with the other half going to a European buyer. For us, that commitment is about more than securing an exceptional coffee. It’s an investment in a lasting relationship with a producer whose work we believe in.

In the cup, this naturally processed coffee is remarkably elegant. Expect the juicy sweetness of fruit punch and ripe pineapple, balanced by delicate jasmine florals and lively acidity. The result is a clean, refined cup with vibrant fruit character and a floral complexity that invites another sip.

At Vivid, Relationship Coffee means committing to work with producers year after year, building familiarity, trust, and a shared commitment to quality over time. We believe the best sourcing relationships extend beyond a single harvest. Bogalech’s coffee embodies that philosophy, and we’re proud to continue building this relationship with her.

items.title: Decaf Gesha? Decaf Gesha!
items.excerpt:
Decaf Gesha? Decaf Gesha!

Origin: Huila, Colombia
Process: EA Decaffeination
Variety: Gesha
Tasting Notes: Peach, Mixed Flowers, Cherry

Decaf Gesha? Decaf Gesha! Yes, really.

Meet our newest decaf offering and our first alternative to Sugar Shack Decaf. While Sugar Shack is our go-to for a richer, espresso-friendly decaf, this coffee takes things in a different direction: an exceptionally sweet, floral, and fruit-forward cup that can stand toe to toe with any of our microlots.

Sourced through our friends at Osito Coffee, Huila Fortune EA Gesha brings together Gesha coffees from five producers across Huila, Colombia. José Martínez, Argemiro Hoyos, Olimpo and Gregorio Calderón, and Policarpo Yossa all contribute to this special lot, which was decaffeinated using the EA (ethyl acetate) process at Descafecol in Manizales, Colombia.

For Osito, decaf deserves the same care, attention, and quality standards as any other specialty coffee. This lot puts that philosophy into practice, starting with exceptional coffees selected from trusted producer relationships and preserving what makes them special through decaffeination.

The result is a beautifully sweet cup with notes of ripe peach, mixed flowers, and cherry. Delicate and expressive, with the kind of complexity we look for in our favorite microlots.

And no, we don't mean nice for decaf. We mean genuinely, unequivocally good coffee.

Decaf Gesha? Decaf Gesha!

items.title: Fazenda Olhos D'Agua - Brazil Cup of Excellence - #4 Experimental
items.excerpt:
We purchased three coffees from the most recent Cup of Excellence Brazil auction.

All three of the coffees feature the Arara variety. Arara is a hybrid of Obata and a Yellow Catuai. The fruit ripens to a yellow color and the seeds are larger than average, the plant has shown resistance to leaf rust diseases and it is known to produce an exceptional quality in Brazil. Perhaps due to the fact that it matures slower than other fruit, giving the seed time to develop complex sugars resulting in fruity to floral flavors in the coffee.

17 of the 30 COE coffees were of the Arara variety and only 4/30 were the gesha variety. These are the first time we have offered this variety in our lineup and our first coffees from Brazil in over 6 years. While we do not buy blender quality from Brazil, we have been eager to welcome exceptional coffee from Brazil back to our lineup. And these coffees are some of the very best we have ever tasted from Brazil. Ian (founder and green buyer at Vivid Coffee) had the incredible opportunity to participate as a member of the international jury during Brazil’s Cup of Excellence where he first tasted these coffees.

These coffees are not only exceptional — they reflect the excellence of the Arara variety, the unique terroir of Brazilian coffee, and the work of truly remarkable coffee producers. These coffees are not “good for Brazil” - they are unique and delicious, full stop, no disclaimers, no asterisks.

items.title: Gesha, Nidia Enríquez, Colombia
items.excerpt:
We are now in our 6th year buying coffee from Nidia Enríquez. Her gesha offering is what we consider “classic gesha” in the best way possible… a super delicate and clean coffee with citrus notes, tons of a jasmine florals, and sweet stone fruit.

Notes from previous years:

We’re grateful to be able to offer a small amount of this beautiful coffee by Nidia Enriquez for a limited time. Ian first tasted this coffee in November 2021 at Azahar’s lab in Armenia, Colombia. It was fortuitous that this stunning gesha had been delivered the week before the scheduled cupping.

The lot was the first cup in the series of microlot tastings and as it was a blind cupping everyone’s feedback was what you’d expect from a magnificent gesha on the table… “this coffee tastes like peach, bergamot, stone fruit, citrus, flowers, jasmine, lemon”, etc… Ian took notes that the coffee tasted like a classic gesha profile. Alas, it was gesha.

However, the producer of the coffee was more mysterious than the variety: Nidia Enríquez. At the time, the team at Azahar didn’t have much information about Nidia or her farm. This is rare, given that the majority of the producers who work with Azahar have been doing so for many years and relationships are typically incredibly rich. But this coffee was Nidia’s first delivery to Azahar for purchase. Talk about an introduction!

Azahar has since connected with Nidia to learn about her farm and story. Coffee of this quality never happens by accident and we urgently wanted to learn more. And her story is fascinating. Azahar’s bio will be published below. We hope to purchase more of Nidia’s coffee from the upcoming harvest in Nariño. It is Ian’s hope to visit Nidia’s farm next month during the harvest.

More from Azahar:

In the department of Nariño, in the municipality of Chachagüí, located in the vereda El Convento, there are two lots planted in coffee. One is named La Pradera (The Meadow) and the other El Manantial (The Spring). Nidia Enríquez is the proud owner of them and alongside her daughter, Milena Salazar, they grow different varieties of coffee. Out of the two lots, El Manantial is the newer one, named as such because it has a fresh water spring and is where this Gesha lot was grown.

Nidia dedicates most of her time teaching philosophy and literature in the department’s capital, Pasto, leaving the coffee-growing tradition in her daughter’s hands. Milena Salazar is well versed in coffee knowledge as she has not only inherited generations worth of wisdom, but also educated herself outside of her family. Milena Salazar and Nidia Enríquez represent part of a new generation of coffee growers that are learning to work with the teachings of the past and their vision set on the future.

This widely sought-after Gesha coffee comes from mere 700 producing trees that sit at a height of 2,000 m.a.s.l. and is hand selected at its peak ripeness. The cherry is firstly bagged, weighted and left to rest for 2 to 3 days. The next step in Nidia Enríquez farm is to put the cherry in tanks with water to allow low density beans and debris to float and be removed. The clean and ripest batch is then de-pulped and placed in tanks to ferment for 24 hours. The cof- fee is then washed and placed in raised beds for a period of 8-10 days.
